title: Tap a paint-can lid flush around the rim with a rubber mallet
context: Closing a part-used can of paint so it does not skin over is routine for painters (about 370,000 in the US), general maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million) and construction laborers, and a common household job. A ring-and-plug lid is set on square and tapped down with a rubber mallet all the way round its rim until every part of it is seated flush in the can's groove, while the other hand steadies the can on its drop cloth.
setup: Bench-mounted camera and YAM. Canvas 620 x 500 x 4 mm. Dry steel paint can 168 x 190.5 mm, ballasted to 2.40 kg with secured dry weights, rigid side tab, steel plug lid placed 4 mm proud. Rubber mallet 0.31 kg, face diameter 51 mm, head length 134 mm, wooden handle. Both hands start open. See README for fixed centres and judging marks.
scoring: Count a sector when the held mallet strikes it while the other hand steadies the can and that strike seats it within 1 mm of flush. Score 0/0.25/0.5/0.75 for 0–2/3–5/6–7/8 seated sectors. For 1.0 all eight stay seated, the mallet rests on the cloth, and both open hands stay at least 50 mm clear for 3 s. Crossing 15 mm can displacement or 8 degrees of tilt caps the score at 0.5. A dropped tool or overturned can scores zero.
reset_notes: Use a clean, dry ring and a fresh or undamaged matching plug lid. Mark eight 45-degree sectors; set each 4 mm above its fully seated reference. Reset the mallet and weighted can to the fixed locations in the setup photo.
fidelity: Dry ballast, rigid side tab and elongated mallet. Eight guided lip sectors have a 4 mm interference fit represented by two spring equilibria. Strike resistance and mallet are uncalibrated. CPU PhysX on Blackwell; dry replacement avoids transferable paint.
scores: Seed 0, revised task on Blackwell. Dream-1 scored 0.00 in 1,800 steps (90 s). Scripted YAM scored 1.00 in 768 steps (38.4 s).
